summary: Your resting heart rate is higher than your usual range.
self_care:
Sit or lie down and rest for 10 minutes.
Drink water if you have not had any recently.
Measure the heart rate again after 10 minutes.
Note any dizziness, chest discomfort or breathlessness in the notes.

summary: Your resting heart rate is lower than your usual range.
self_care:
Check that you are not asleep or just woken.
Measure the heart rate again after 10 minutes.
Note any dizziness or feeling faint in the notes.

summary: Your heart rate is very high at rest, which can have serious causes and needs prompt advice.
self_care:
Stop any exercise and sit or lie down now.
Measure again in 5 minutes.
If you have chest pain, fainting, confusion or trouble breathing, treat it as an emergency.
protocol:
Tell the crew medical officer now and share this reading.
Use the onboard checklist for a fast heart rate and chest discomfort.
Measure every 10 minutes and log each value.
Send the readings to ground and wait for their advice.
Do not return to exercise until ground or the crew medical officer agrees.

summary: Your heart rate is very low at rest, which needs prompt advice.
self_care:
Sit or lie down now.
Measure again in 5 minutes.
If you faint, feel confused or have chest pain, treat it as an emergency.
protocol:
Tell the crew medical officer now.
Stay with a crew member.
Measure every 10 minutes and log each value.
Send the readings to ground and follow their advice.

summary: Your blood pressure is above the usual range for you.
self_care:
Sit quietly for 5 minutes and measure again.
Avoid caffeine and heavy exercise until the next check.
Note any headache or vision changes in the notes.

summary: Your blood pressure is lower than usual.
self_care:
Sit or lie down and drink water if you can.
Stand up slowly.
Measure again in 15 minutes.

summary: Your blood pressure is very high, which needs medical advice now.
self_care:
Sit or lie down quietly and avoid exertion.
Measure again in 10 minutes.
If you have a severe headache, chest pain, vision changes, weakness or confusion, treat it as an emergency.
protocol:
Tell the crew medical officer now and share the readings.
Repeat the measurement every 10 minutes and log each value.
Avoid exercise and follow the onboard checklist for high blood pressure.
Send the readings and symptoms to ground and follow their advice while you wait.

summary: Your blood pressure is very low, which can cause fainting.
self_care:
Lie down with your feet slightly raised.
Drink water if you can.
Measure again in 10 minutes.
If you faint, feel confused or cannot stand, treat it as an emergency.
protocol:
Tell the crew medical officer now.
Stay with a crew member.
Repeat the measurement every 10 minutes and log each value.
Send the readings to ground and follow their advice.

summary: Your lower blood pressure number is above the usual range.
self_care:
Rest for 5 minutes and measure again.
Read the top number as well, and note both in the log.

summary: Your lower blood pressure number is below the usual range.
self_care:
Rest and drink water.
Measure again in 15 minutes.
Note any dizziness in the notes.

summary: Your blood oxygen is lower than usual.
self_care:
Sit upright and breathe slowly and deeply.
Check that the probe is on a warm finger, then measure again in 5 minutes.
Note any breathlessness or cough in the notes.

summary: Your blood oxygen is very low, which needs urgent attention.
self_care:
Sit upright and stay still.
Measure again in 2 minutes with the probe on a warm finger.
If you have chest pain, confusion or trouble breathing, treat it as an emergency.
protocol:
Tell the crew medical officer now.
Check the cabin air and breathing equipment with the crew.
Measure every 5 minutes and log each value.
Send the readings to ground and follow their advice.

summary: Your temperature is above the usual range, which can have several causes such as infection or dehydration.
self_care:
Rest and drink water.
Measure again in 1 hour.
Note any chills, sore throat or cough in the notes.

summary: Your temperature is below the usual range.
self_care:
Warm up under a blanket and rest.
Measure again in 30 minutes.
Note any shivering or confusion in the notes.

summary: Your temperature is high, which needs medical advice now.
self_care:
Rest, drink water and loosen clothing.
Measure again in 30 minutes.
If you have confusion, a stiff neck or trouble breathing, treat it as an emergency.
protocol:
Tell the crew medical officer now.
Use the onboard checklist for fever.
Measure every 30 minutes and log each value.
Send the readings and symptoms to ground and follow their advice before taking any medicine.

summary: Your temperature is very low, which needs urgent attention.
self_care:
Get warm under blankets and rest.
Measure again in 30 minutes.
If you are drowsy, confused or cannot stay awake, treat it as an emergency.
protocol:
Tell the crew medical officer now.
Stay with a crew member.
Rewarm slowly with blankets and the onboard kit.
Measure every 30 minutes and log each value.
Send the readings to ground and follow their advice.

summary: Your blood sugar is higher than the usual range.
self_care:
Drink water.
Measure again in 1 to 2 hours.
Note how long it has been since you last ate, in the notes.

summary: Your blood sugar is lower than the usual range.
self_care:
Eat a small snack with some carbohydrate, such as crackers or fruit.
Measure again in 15 minutes.
Note any shakiness or sweating in the notes.

summary: Your blood sugar is very high, which needs medical advice now.
self_care:
Drink water and hold food until you have advice.
Measure again in 1 hour.
If you are very thirsty, confused or drowsy, treat it as an emergency.
protocol:
Tell the crew medical officer now.
Do not change any medicine dose without ground advice.
Measure every hour and log each value.
Send the readings and symptoms to ground and follow their advice.

summary: Your blood sugar is very low, which can cause confusion and collapse.
self_care:
If you are awake and can swallow safely, take fast sugar such as glucose tablets or juice now.
Measure again in 15 minutes.
If you are confused, drowsy or cannot swallow, treat it as an emergency.
protocol:
Tell the crew medical officer now and stay with a crew member.
Repeat the measurement every 15 minutes and log each value.
Give more fast sugar only if the astronaut can swallow safely, as the onboard checklist says.
Send the readings to ground and follow their advice.

summary: You slept less than your usual range, which can slow reactions and lower mood.
self_care:
Plan a short nap in the next 24 hours if the schedule allows.
Keep the sleep area dark and quiet.
Limit caffeine in the second half of the waking day.

summary: You slept more than your usual range, which can be a sign of fatigue or illness.
self_care:
Note how you felt on waking in the notes.
Check your other readings for today.

summary: Your mood is lower than usual.
self_care:
Talk with a crew member or the ground support team today.
Do one activity you enjoy this evening.
If low mood lasts more than two days, ask for a private call with the behavioural health team.

summary: Your reaction time is slower than usual, which can raise the risk of mistakes.
self_care:
Pause tasks that need quick reactions.
Repeat the reaction test after a 10 minute break.
If the test stays slow, tell the flight team before doing critical tasks.

summary: You exercised less than your target, and less loading can speed bone and muscle loss in microgravity.
self_care:
Plan a session of at least 30 minutes before the day ends.
Split it into two shorter sessions if needed.
Note the reason in the notes.

summary: Your body mass is lower than your usual range, which can be a sign of low food intake.
self_care:
Eat your scheduled meals and snacks.
Weigh again tomorrow at the same time.
Note any loss of appetite or nausea in the notes.

summary: Your body mass is higher than your usual range, which can be due to fluid or food.
self_care:
Weigh again tomorrow at the same time.
Note any swelling or unusual fluid intake in the notes.

summary: Your back pain is above the usual level, which can disturb sleep and work.
self_care:
Change position and use the supported sitting or lying posture from the crew handbook.
Do gentle stretching only if it does not increase the pain.
Note where the pain is and when it started in the notes.

summary: You have eaten less than the usual daily range.
self_care:
Eat a planned meal or snack with some protein soon.
Try your favourite foods from the food list.
Log everything you eat so the total is accurate.
If it happens for several days, mention appetite in the notes.

summary: You have drunk less than the usual daily range.
self_care:
Drink a pouch of water now.
Sip often through the day instead of all at once.
Check the colour of your next urine: dark means drink more.

summary: You report symptoms of illness.
self_care:
Take your temperature.
Rest and drink fluids.
Wipe shared surfaces and keep away from other crew where you can.
Note every symptom and when it started.

summary: You report severe symptoms of illness, which can spread to the crew and needs prompt advice.
self_care:
Take your temperature and rest now.
Wear a mask and keep away from other crew.
If you have trouble breathing, a spreading rash or confusion, treat it as an emergency.
protocol:
Tell the crew medical officer now and isolate in a separate module if possible.
Follow the onboard checklist for fever and infection.
Measure temperature and heart rate every 4 hours and log them.
Send symptoms and readings to ground and follow their treatment advice.
Clean shared surfaces and tell the crew to wash hands and report symptoms.

summary: Your stress is higher than usual.
self_care:
Take a 10 minute break from your task.
Do some slow breathing: in for 4 seconds, out for 6.
Talk with a crew member about what is weighing on you.
If stress lasts more than two days, ask for a private call with the behavioural health team.

summary: Your stress is very high, which can harm sleep and judgement.
self_care:
Stop and take a break from non-urgent work.
Talk to someone you trust now.
Ask for a private call with the behavioural health team.
protocol:
Tell the crew medical officer that stress is very high.
Ask the commander to move non-urgent tasks off your schedule.
Arrange a private call with the behavioural health team.
Check sleep and mood over the last 3 days.
Check in again within 24 hours.

summary: You feel less connected than usual.
self_care:
Share a meal with a crew member today.
Send a message or video to someone at home.
Join a group activity this evening.

summary: You feel very isolated, which can come before low mood and conflict.
self_care:
Talk to a crew member now, or ask someone to sit with you.
Ask for a private call with the behavioural health team.
Say how you feel in the notes.
protocol:
Tell the crew medical officer that you feel very isolated.
Arrange a private call with the behavioural health team.
Plan a shared meal or activity for each day this week.
Check mood and sleep and check in again within 24 hours.

summary: Your near vision is blurrier than usual. Some astronauts develop a far-sighted shift on long missions.
self_care:
Repeat the test in good light with your reading glasses on.
Check the card step and the 40 cm distance.
Note any blur, headache or eye strain in the notes.
Tell the flight surgeon about any change from your own baseline.

summary: Your near vision is much worse than usual, which can be a sign of spaceflight eye changes (SANS).
self_care:
Repeat the test once in good light.
Tell the crew medical officer today, do not wait.
Note when the blur started and whether it is one eye or both.
protocol:
Tell the crew medical officer and the flight surgeon now.
Repeat the other eye test (near vision and Amsler grid) and note which eye is affected.
Use the onboard eye exam tools (acuity, Amsler grid, fundus photos, OCT) as ground directs.
Send the results to ground and follow their advice on further imaging.

summary: You marked some squares as wavy, blurred, dark or missing.
self_care:
Repeat the test once for the eye that was affected.
Check you looked at the centre dot, at the right distance, in good light.
Note where the distortion is and what it looks like.
Tell the flight surgeon about any distortion, even if it is small.

summary: You marked many distorted squares, which needs prompt medical advice.
self_care:
Repeat the test once with the affected eye.
Tell the crew medical officer today, do not wait.
Do not rub or press on the eye.
protocol:
Tell the crew medical officer and the flight surgeon now.
Repeat the other eye test (near vision and Amsler grid) and note which eye is affected.
Use the onboard eye exam tools (acuity, Amsler grid, fundus photos, OCT) as ground directs.
Send the results to ground and follow their advice on further imaging.

summary: You feel dizzy or unsteady more than usual.
self_care:
Move your head slowly and use handholds.
Stay still with your eyes closed for a few minutes.
Drink water and eat a light meal.
Note what set it off in the notes.

summary: Severe dizziness or nausea can stop you working safely and needs advice.
self_care:
Stop any task that needs balance or care and hold on to a handhold.
Rest with your head still.
If you vomit or cannot keep fluids down, tell the crew now.
protocol:
Tell the crew medical officer now.
Check fluids and sleep, and list any anti-nausea medicine already taken.
Rate it again every 2 hours and log each rating.
Send the log to ground and follow their advice before any critical task.

summary: Your urine is darker than usual, a sign you may need more fluid.
self_care:
Drink a pouch of water now.
Sip regularly over the next few hours.
Check the colour again at your next break.

summary: Very dark urine suggests dehydration, and low fluid raises kidney stone risk.
self_care:
Drink water now and keep drinking over the next hour.
Rest and stop heavy exercise until the colour is lighter.
If you have pain in your side, blood in the urine or a fever, tell the crew now.
protocol:
Tell the crew medical officer now.
Log fluid intake and urine colour every 2 hours.
Ask about pain in the side or lower belly, and blood in the urine.
Send the log to ground; they may advise a kidney stone check.

summary: Your grip is weaker than usual.
self_care:
Repeat the test after a short rest.
Check how many resistive exercise sessions you did this week.
Note any pain or numbness in the hand or arm.
